rounds.fact: Yelp started in 2004 as an email-based referral service before pivoting to the review-website format it's known for today, after users kept asking for a public place to post reviews.
Orbitz was launched in 2001 by a group of major airlines banding together to compete directly with Expedia and Travelocity for online bookings.
GameSpot launched in 1996 and became known for its numerical review scores becoming a genuine influence on game sales, sometimes controversially so.
Slack was built from the internal chat tool of Glitch, a whimsical MMO that shut down in 2012. The aubergine sidebar became so iconic that its 2019 rebrand made headlines.
Digg pioneered the user-voted news-aggregation format years before Reddit took over that space, and a single controversial 2010 redesign is often cited as the reason it lost most of its audience.
